arguments.document_type: Emergency Motion for Extension of Time to File Response
arguments.content:
MEMORANDUM IN SUPPORT OF EMERGENCY MOTION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME TO FILE RESPONSE

I. Introduction

Due to an ongoing scheduled maintenance window affecting the court electronic filing gateway (Asset: court-filing-gateway-01, Maintenance Window: MW-2026-LEG-003, 01:00–05:00 UTC), counsel has been unable to electronically file the responsive pleading in the above-captioned matter. This emergency motion seeks a brief extension of time under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 6(b) to ensure the client’s rights are preserved.

II. Factual and Legal Basis

Pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 6(b), the court may extend a deadline upon a showing of good cause. The maintenance event was pre-scheduled and approved by the operations team; however, it directly impacts the firm’s ability to file electronically during the critical window before the current deadline. Failure to file could result in dismissal under Rule 12(b)(6) standards, as clarified in Ashcroft v. Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662 (2009), where a complaint must state a plausible claim. Here, the defense is not waiving any rights but seeks to avoid procedural default due to technical inaccessibility beyond counsel’s control.

III. Request for Relief

Counsel respectfully requests a 24-hour extension from the current deadline to file the responsive pleading, which will allow submission once the filing system is restored. All other deadlines shall be adjusted accordingly.

Respectfully submitted,

[Attorney Signature Block]
